title: Recursion & Call Stack
syllabus_note: Additional DS Concept (Foundational extension beyond prescribed lab syllabus)
definition: Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a computational problem by calling a copy of itself with a smaller subproblem until a terminating base case is reached.

principles.base_case: The condition under which the function terminates without making further recursive calls, preventing infinite recursion.
principles.recursive_step: The reduction step where the problem is broken down into one or more smaller instances of the same problem.
principles.call_stack: Each recursive call pushes an activation record (stack frame) onto the system call stack storing local variables and return addresses.

space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary call stack space proportional to the maximum recursion depth.
applications: Divide and Conquer algorithms (Merge Sort, Quick Sort)
Graph DFS and Backtracking (N-Queens, Sudoku solver, Maze pathfinding)

viva_questions.question: What happens if a recursive function does not have a base case?
viva_questions.answer: The function calls itself indefinitely until the system runtime stack exhausts its allocated memory, causing a fatal Stack Overflow exception or segmentation fault.

viva_questions.question: How many total moves are required to solve Tower of Hanoi for n disks?
viva_questions.answer: 2^n - 1 moves. For n = 3 disks, exactly 7 moves are required; for n = 4, 15 moves are required.
